review_candidates.title: Project Risk Manager - EMEA
review_candidates.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Project Risk Manager - EMEA based in United Kingdom. Lead risk management across a complex EMEA project portfolio supporting the delivery of large-scale AI infrastructure. You will establish consistent risk governance while providing hands-on expertise across project, portfolio, commercial, cost, and schedule risk. Working alongside project directors, engineers, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operations teams, you will help make uncertainty visible and actionable. You will lead qualitative and quantitative risk analysis, including Monte Carlo simulations, schedule risk analysis, scenario modelling, and contingency assessment. The role combines independent assurance with close business partnership, giving you influence over major project and investment decisions. You will identify systemic and correlated risks across the regional portfolio and translate complex analysis into clear recommendations for senior leadership. This is a high-impact opportunity for an experienced risk professional who thrives in fast-paced, technically complex, and rapidly scaling infrastructure environments. Accountabilities Lead the regional project risk management programme across the EMEA portfolio, establishing consistent governance, standards, processes, methodologies, and escalation requirements. Embed risk management throughout the project lifecycle and across Engineering, Procurement, Construction, Project Controls, Commercial, Commissioning, and Operations Readiness. Provide independent risk oversight and constructive challenge to project and functional leadership, ensuring significant risks and opportunities receive appropriate attention. Promote a proactive risk culture based on early identification, clear ownership, accountability, timely escalation, and risk-informed decision-making. Act as the regional subject matter expert and trusted adviser on project and portfolio risk for project, regional, and executive leadership. Lead the identification, assessment, mitigation, monitoring, escalation, and closure of project risks and opportunities. Build, maintain, and oversee project risk registers, ensuring material risks have clear owners, mitigation strategies, action plans, residual assessments, and escalation paths. Assess delivery risks across design, permitting, grid connection, procurement, long-lead equipment, construction, commercial and contractual performance, commissioning, energisation, and capacity delivery. Consolidate project-level risks at regional level to identify emerging, systemic, correlated, and concentration risks requiring portfolio-wide action. Promote the identification and realization of opportunities relating to cost, schedule, standardisation, procurement, constructability, and overall project execution. Lead qualitative and quantitative cost and schedule risk analysis, including Monte Carlo simulation, Schedule Risk Analysis (SRA), scenario analysis, and other probabilistic techniques. Assess cost exposure, schedule uncertainty, critical-path risks, key milestones, and confidence in achieving committed delivery and ready-for-service dates. Develop risk-based recommendations for project contingency and management reserves and support governance over their utilization and release. Analyse regional risk drivers, correlations, scenarios, and sensitivities to identify potential portfolio impacts and mitigation priorities. Provide risk analysis and recommendations for investment decisions, stage gates, baseline approvals, major contract awards, and other significant project decisions. Produce concise project and regional reporting covering top risks and opportunities, emerging exposures, trends, mitigation effectiveness, contingency status, and matters requiring escalation. Develop risk dashboards and analytics that provide visibility into exposure, trends, concentrations, and confidence across cost, schedule, commissioning, and capacity commitments. Monitor mitigation progress, overdue actions, changes in exposure, realised risks, and significant issues requiring project, regional, or executive attention. Conduct periodic project risk reviews and health checks to assess the quality and effectiveness of risk identification, analysis, mitigation, reporting, and governance. Independently test project assumptions, forecasts, contingency requirements, mitigation strategies, and confidence levels to ensure material exposures are understood and communicated appropriately. Identify recurring risks, systemic weaknesses, successful mitigation strategies, and lessons learned across projects and incorporate them into future delivery approaches. Drive continuous improvement across risk processes, methodologies, tools, analytics, reporting, and organisational risk capability. Requirements Degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, Business, Finance, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant industry experience. Significant professional experience in risk management, project controls, or project delivery within complex EPC, construction, infrastructure, energy, mission-critical, or major capital programmes. Demonstrated experience leading project and portfolio risk management, including identification, assessment, mitigation, monitoring, escalation, and assurance. Strong understanding of cost, schedule, contingency, and project controls principles and how they integrate with project risk management. Advanced experience applying quantitative risk analysis and probabilistic techniques to assess project cost and schedule uncertainty. Strong hands-on experience with Monte Carlo simulation, cost and schedule risk analysis, scenario analysis, and risk-based contingency development. Strong understanding of EPC contracting, procurement, supply chain, change management, claims, and commercial risk. Proven ability to influence and constructively challenge senior project and functional leaders in complex, fast-moving environments. Excellent written, verbal, facilitation, and executive communication skills, with the ability to translate complex risk information into clear business insights and recommended actions. Ability to identify systemic and correlated risks across multiple projects and provide regional-level insight to support management decisions. Experience delivering hyperscale, AI, mission-critical, or large-scale data centre programmes is advantageous. Familiarity with power, cooling, grid connections, long-lead equipment, commissioning, and capacity delivery is a plus. Experience with enterprise or project risk management platforms and their integration with scheduling, cost management, and reporting systems is beneficial. Relevant professional certification such as PMI-RMP, PMP, APM PMQ or ChPP, AACE International, IRM, or an equivalent risk or project management credential is advantageous. Working knowledge of recognised risk management frameworks, including ISO 31000 and PMBOK, with familiarity with standards such as ISO 9001, ISO 45001, and ISO 14001. Experience presenting portfolio risk, contingency, schedule confidence, and emerging exposures to executive leadership or governance committees. Experience with @Risk, Riskonnect, Safran, or comparable industry-standard risk management tools is a plus. Strong analytical thinking, sound judgement, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills. Benefits Competitive salary based on the scope and value of the role rather than previous compensation. Equity opportunity, allowing eligible employees to participate in the organisation's long-term growth. Discretionary bonus opportunity. Retirement or pension contributions. Comprehensive health, wellbeing, and insurance benefits. Generous annual vacation allowance. Fully remote working environment within Europe. Opportunity to work on large-scale AI infrastructure and major capital projects. High-impact role with significant exposure to regional and executive-level decision-making. Collaborative environment focused on professional development, trust, autonomy, and sustainable work-life balance. Opportunity to contribute to the development of risk management practices across a rapidly scaling international infrastructure portfolio. review_candidates.title: Incident & Change Manager
review_candidates.description: Australia's Leading Managed Service Provider | Own, Improve & Lead Critical Service Functions We're looking for an experienced Incident & Change Manager to take ownership of two important operational functions at First Focus. This isn't a role where you simply follow established processes, coordinate incidents and administer change. We're looking for someone who will own these functions, challenge how we currently operate, identify what isn't working and make them better . You'll have the autonomy to shape Incident and Change Management at First Focus, while remaining hands-on when major incidents occur. If you enjoy solving problems, improving how things work, influencing people and taking ownership of outcomes, this could be a great role for you. The Role Reporting to the Head of Service Delivery, you'll be accountable for the effectiveness and continuous improvement of our Incident and Change Management functions. That means you'll: Lead major incident response, bringing together the right people, coordinating decisions and actions, managing communications and driving incidents through to resolution Improve the quality of Incident Management, including auditing incidents, ensuring strong Post Incident Reviews, identifying recurring issues and driving actions that reduce the likelihood and impact of future incidents Own the effectiveness of Change Management, ensuring appropriate standards and controls are in place, identifying risk and failure trends, and improving the process through better ways of working, automation and operational insight Drive improvement across both functions, working with teams across the business to turn identified problems and opportunities into practical improvements. What Matters To Us Ownership matters. You'll be accountable for the performance and maturity of these functions - not simply for delivering the day-to-day activities within them. We need someone who takes responsibility for identifying issues, creating opportunities and driving improvement. Curiosity matters. We want someone who naturally questions how things work, looks for recurring problems and continually asks how we can operate more effectively, consistently and safely. Communication matters. Incident and Change Management require a very high standard of written and verbal communication. You'll need to communicate clearly under pressure, produce high-quality customer-facing documentation and tailor communications to different audiences. Influence matters. You'll often need to achieve outcomes through people you don't directly manage. You'll need to bring the right people together during incidents, challenge when standards aren't being met and build the support required to drive improvements. Requirements What we're looking for You'll be someone who is comfortable taking ownership of operational functions and improving them over time. You don't necessarily need to be an expert in every aspect of Incident and Change Management on day one. Strong experience is valuable, but we're equally interested in someone with the judgement, curiosity, communication skills and drive to learn quickly and become the expert. Most importantly, you're someone who is comfortable working with autonomy, identifying what needs to be done and taking responsibility for getting it done. What You'll Bring Strong experience in Incident Management, Change Management, Service Management or a closely related operational role, ideally including experience with high-priority incidents Excellent written and verbal communication skills, particularly in high-pressure or customer-facing situations Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to coordinate and drive outcomes across teams A demonstrated ability to identify problems, analyse trends and drive practical process and operational improvements Strong judgement, organisation and self-direction, with the confidence to make decisions and challenge the status quo Highly regarded ITIL or relevant Service Management experience Experience in an MSP, IT services or similarly fast-paced operational environment Experience developing Incident or Change Management processes, standards or controls Experience using automation, workflow improvement or operational data to reduce risk and improve efficiency Benefits Why First Focus? You'll receive: Competitive salary package including up to $120,000 + super + other benefits Free access to Uprise, including confidential 1:1 coaching with qualified psychologists and counsellors Flexible hybrid working to support work-life balance Our "Never Stop Growing" program, including 10 paid study days each year, certification exam fees and salary increases for completed certifications (conditions apply) Frequent internal technical training and access to an extensive learning library FastTrack mentoring program Opportunities to work with cutting-edge AI technologies and help shape our AI practice A genuinely supportive culture where people share knowledge rather than hoard it Our MAD (Making A Difference) Council supporting equality, charity and environmental initiatives Option to package a Tesla company car (conditions apply) Regular social events, great people and plenty of laughs along the way Neurodiversity: First Focus welcomes applications from Neurodiverse candidates. We recommend & appreciate disclosure along with the application so that a copy of our Neurodiversity Statement can be provided outlining the flexible options we can offer to best showcase your skills. AI in Recruitment: We use AI-assisted recruitment tools as part of our recruitment process. These tools do not make hiring decisions. Candidate information is handled in accordance with the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).

review_candidates.title: Remote Engineering Expert
review_candidates.description: About Turing: Based in San Francisco, California, Turing is the world’s leading research accelerator for frontier AI labs and a trusted partner for global enterprises deploying advanced AI systems. Turing supports customers in two ways: first, by accelerating frontier research with high-quality data, advanced training pipelines, plus top AI researchers who specialize in coding, reasoning, STEM, multilinguality, multimodality, and agents; and second, by applying that expertise to help enterprises transform AI from proof of concept into proprietary intelligence with systems that perform reliably, deliver measurable impact, and drive lasting results on the P&L. Role Overview: We are seeking experienced AI Evaluation Engineers (Engineering Simulation & Design) to author and validate "model-breaking," simulation-based engineering design problems to train and evaluate state-of-the-art AI agents. Operating across major engineering disciplines—including Electrical, Mechanical, Control Systems, Aerospace, Systems, and Robotics—you will create complex, multi-constraint tasks where AI agents must interpret requirements, navigate trade-offs, configure open-source simulation tools, diagnose failures, and iterate toward valid solutions. You will analyze agent execution logs, expose systemic reasoning gaps, and build automated, objective graders to elevate frontier model performance. Job Requirements: Education & Expertise: Master’s degree or PhD in Electrical, Mechanical, Aerospace, with 10+ years of hands-on engineering design experience. Simulation Tooling: Proficiency with at least one domain-relevant open-source simulation package (e.g., ngspice, PySpice, OpenFOAM, FEniCSx, CalculiX, python-control, CadQuery, build123d, OpenModelica, Cantera, Gmsh) combined with strong Python scripting skills. AI Evaluation & Failure Diagnostics: Hands-on experience with modern LLMs/coding agents and evaluation concepts (pass@k, failure-mode analysis, nondeterministic behavior), with the ability to audit trajectory logs and isolate core reasoning/tool-use failures. Domain Rigor & Precision: Uncompromising attention to physical plausibility, unit consistency, boundary conditions, convergence criteria, and technical documentation. Availability & Commitment: Talent must have weekend on-call availability (part-time engagement is acceptable). Technical Infrastructure: Personal desktop/laptop equipped with a stable, high-speed internet connection in a remote setup. Job Responsibilities: Model-Breaking Problem Design: Author original, self-contained engineering design tasks with competing constraints, explicit optimization targets, validated reference solutions, and objective autograders. Environment & Simulation Integration: Build, run, and validate problem environments using open-source simulation tools and custom Python test benches. Trajectory Analysis & Failure Mode Taxonomy: Evaluate coding agent outputs and execution logs across repeated trials to identify systemic failure modes (e.g., misinterpreting simulator feedback, premature design convergence, physically impossible geometries). Difficulty Calibration & Benchmark Refinement: Iteratively refine problem difficulty based on empirical model performance data without introducing ambiguity or missing information. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with AI researchers, pod leads, and domain experts to integrate high-rigor benchmarks into the model evaluation pipeline. Domains: Electrical Engineering Mechanical Engineering Aerospace Engineering Education & Experience: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience in any field. Experience in AI evaluation, data annotation, content review, quality assurance, or a related analytical role is preferred but not required. Offer Details: Commitments Required: 40 hours per week with 4 hours of overlap with PST. Engagement type: Contractor Engagement Length: upto 24 weeks Evaluation Process: Shortlisted candidates will be sent a Job Interest Form. Finalized talents will go through delivery review & proceeded further accordingly.
